Import an external table of clades as total_richness_per_clades objects

Source: R/import_total_richness_per_clades.R
import_total_richness_per_clades.Rd

Read a table (e.g., a .csv file, or an Excel sheet) with the total number of species per clades, and convert it into the total_richness_per_clades objects ready-to-be-used as input for phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa() and/or phylograftR::graft_missing_clades().

The table is converted by phylograftR::build_total_richness_per_clades(), which matches the clades with those of missing_taxa_list, and checks that the richness is consistent with the full sequence of grafting.

Usage

import_total_richness_per_clades(
  file,
  phy,
  missing_taxa_list,
  sep = NULL,
  sheet = 1,
  reader = NULL,
  return_richness_table = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

file

Character string. Path to the file with the table. The format is chosen from the extension of the file: ".csv" (comma-separated), ".tsv", ".tab" or ".txt" (tab-separated), ".xlsx" or ".xls" (Excel, requires the package readxl). Use sep or reader for other formats.

The table must record one row per clade, with the columns Clade (tips, node ID, or name), total_richness, and, optionally, Clade_name.

  • Clade: a monophyletic group from the backbone phylogeny defined by tips, a node ID, or a name (see Details), from which the total richness is known.

  • total_richness: Total number of species of the clade. It includes the backbone species, all the taxa to graft that belong to the clade, and the unsampled species that are known to exist but will not be grafted. Use NA if unknown.

  • Clade_name (Optional): Name of the clade, used to check matching with other inputs, and to report warnings in downstream functions. If the clade is written with a name in Clade, it is its name.

The columns Target_clade and Target_clade_name, or Sister_clade and Sister_clade_name, are accepted instead of Clade and Clade_name (e.g., for tables prepared for a single grafting function). All the columns are read as text. Blank cells and NA are missing values.

phy

An object of class "phylo". The backbone phylogeny on which the taxa will be grafted. It is used to check the validity of the tips and clades provided.

missing_taxa_list

A missing_taxa_list, or the list of two missing_taxa_list ($taxa and $clades) built for the same backbone phylogeny, e.g., with phylograftR::import_missing_taxa_list() or phylograftR::build_missing_taxa_list_from_taxonomy(). It defines the type(s) of the output, and is used to harmonize the clades and check the validity of the richness values provided.

sep

Character string. Field separator of a text file. Default is NULL, to choose it from the extension of the file: "," for .csv, and a tab for .tsv, .tab and .txt. Commas are also used inside the cells to separate the tips: to distinguish from the field separator, the cells containing tips must be quoted.

sheet

Character string or integer. Only used for Excel files. Name or position of the sheet to read. Default is 1.

reader

Function. Optional function used to read file, to import any other format (e.g., .ods, or an export of an online spreadsheet). It must take the path of the file as first argument and return a data frame. If provided, it is used whatever the extension of the file. Default is NULL.

return_richness_table

Logical. Whether to return the expected richness and sampling fraction of each clade in the attribute "richness_table" of the output. It is computed before any grafting, from the backbone, the missing_taxa_list and the total richness. It is a tool to examine a priori the sampling fraction expected in each clade. The actual effective sampling fractions of the grafted phylogenies, accessible with phylograftR::extract_sampling_info(), may differ (see 'Richness table' in Details). Default is TRUE.

verbose

Logical. Whether to print the conversions of node IDs into tips (if any), and a summary of the table. Default is TRUE.

...

Further arguments passed to the function reading the file (utils::read.table() for text files, readxl::read_excel() for Excel files, or reader).

Value

If file contains one type of taxa, a total_richness_per_clades list; if it contains both types ($taxa and $clades), a list with two total_richness_per_clades named $taxa (for phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa()) and $clades (for phylograftR::graft_missing_clades()).

Each total_richness_per_clades list contains all the clades of the table, and has the following items:

  • $Target_clade (or $Sister_clade, for the list of missing clades) List of character vectors of tips defining the clades.

  • $Target_clade_name (or $Sister_clade_name) Only if some clades have a name. Character vector (NA if a clade has no name).

  • $total_richness Integer vector of the total richness of the clades (NA if unknown).

If return_richness_table = TRUE, the output has the attribute "richness_table", a data.frame with one row per clade: Clade_name, Clade_tips, total_richness_provided (the value of the table), total_richness (as used for the grafting, derived from the nested clades if unknown), nb_backbone_species, nb_missing_species (all the taxa to graft in the clade, of both types), nb_unsampled_species, and sampling_fraction ((nb_backbone_species + nb_missing_species) / total_richness), the expected sampling fraction before grafting (see phylograftR::build_total_richness_per_clades()). Without it, the output does not have this attribute.

Details

Identifying clades

Clades can be defined by tips, a node ID, or a name:

  • A pair of tips defines the clade as their MRCA node (e.g., "t26, t18"), separated by commas. A single tip defines the "clade" as the terminal branch of this tip. Tip labels must include at least one other character than digits.

  • A node ID of phy (digits only, e.g., "34") also defines the clade, as in phylograftR::build_missing_taxa_list().

  • A single value that is not a tip of phy is a clade name (e.g., "Family_A"). Names are matched with the names of the clades of missing_taxa_list ($Target_clade_name, $Sister_clade_name, and the names of the excluded subclades) and, for lists built from taxonomic tables, with all the taxonomic groups of the backbone taxonomy. The taxonomic groups are stored in the attribute "taxonomic_groups" of the object returned by phylograftR::build_missing_taxa_list_from_taxonomy(): they are only available if missing_taxa_list is this object itself, not one of its elements ($taxa or $clades) alone.

Clades are matched by their MRCA node in phy: a clade can only be listed once, and the tips written in the output are those already used in missing_taxa_list for the same clade, so the tips match in all the objects. The grafting functions require all the clades used in missing_taxa_list to be listed: the clades that are not in the table are added with an unknown richness (NA), and their number is reported.

Unsampled species

For a focal clade with a total_richness value provided: total_richness = nb_backbone + nb_missing + nb_unsampled, with nb_missing the number of lineages to graft within the focal clade, and nb_unsampled the number of species in this clade that are not represented in the backbone, nor will be grafted, but must be accounted in the sampling fraction for when fitting diversification models.

For a clade with no total_richness value (NA or NULL), nb_unsampled are estimated as the sum of nb_unsampled over the largest clades nested within it with a total_richness value provided. If there is none, nb_unsampled = 0. The rationale is that even if nb_unsampled cannot be derived from its total_richness (as it is not provided for this clade), it has to at least account for the nb_unsampled species that have being identified in its own nested clades.

Full sequence of grafting

The same table is valid for the grafting of the taxa within target clades and for the grafting of the missing clades as sister to backbone clades, in either order. With the recommended sequence (taxa first, then missing clades on the grafted phylogeny):

  • When the taxa are grafted, the taxa to graft as missing clades are not in the backbone nor in the list, so they are counted among the unsampled species of the clades.

  • When the missing clades are grafted, the taxa grafted before are tips of the backbone, and the unsampled species are the species still unaccounted for.

The function checks the richness against all the taxa to graft at once: the function stops if the total richness of a clade is lower than the number of species it contains (backbone species and all the taxa to graft within it, or within clades nested within it), or if a clade has fewer unsampled species than the clades with a total richness nested within it.

Richness table

With return_richness_table = TRUE, the output has the attribute "richness_table": a data.frame that reports, before any grafting, the richness and the sampling fraction expected in each clade (see Value for details on its columns). It can be used to examine a priori the sampling fraction of the clades and to spot errors in the total richness: e.g., an unlikely low sampling fraction, or clades with an unknown richness (NA) for which unsampled species were derived from nested clades, or assumed to be none. It can also be used to compare the sampling of different clades, or to decide which clades need a better estimate of their richness.

The sampling fractions of the table are expectations, and the effective sampling fractions of the grafted phylogenies may differ. The table assumes that all the taxa to graft end up in the clade where they belong: a taxon counts for all the clades that are, or enclose, its target clade, and a missing clade counts for the clades that enclose its sister clade (it is grafted on the stem of the sister clade, so not within the sister clade itself). However, where taxa are actually grafted varies among the grafted phylogenies (and among the stochastic maps, if any): a taxon can be grafted on the stem of its target clade, which is outside of the clade, or within a clade nested in its target clade, which changes the richness of these clades. The actual effective richness and sampling fraction of each clade, in each grafted phylogeny, are extracted a posteriori with phylograftR::extract_sampling_info() on the output of the grafting functions, using the same total_richness_per_clades.

See also

Other functions from phylograftR:

  • phylograftR::build_total_richness_per_clades() to convert a data.frame of clades already loaded in R.

  • phylograftR::import_missing_taxa_list() to read the table of missing taxa from an external file.

  • phylograftR::import_taxonomic_table() to read taxonomic tables from external files.

  • phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa() and phylograftR::graft_missing_clades() to graft the taxa using the richness.

Author

Examples

# Path to an example table of the total richness of clades, provided with the package
file_path <- system.file("extdata", "toy_total_richness.csv", package = "phylograftR")
read.csv(file_path)
#>   Target_clade Target_clade_name total_richness
#> 1      t26,t18          Family_A             25
#> 2       t8,t22          Family_B             NA
#> 3        t8,t7         Subfam_B1             14
#> 4           t5             Gen_2             NA
#> 5       t5,t12          Tribe_B2              8

# Load the backbone, and the list of missing taxa associated with the table
data(toy_backbone)
data(toy_missing_taxa_list)

# Import it as a 'total_richness_per_clades' object, checked against the backbone and the list
total_richness_per_clades <- import_total_richness_per_clades(
    file = file_path,
    phy = toy_backbone,
    missing_taxa_list = toy_missing_taxa_list)
#> 5 clade(s) in total richness: 3 with a value, 2 with an unknown richness. See attr(, "richness_table") for the expected sampling fraction of the clades.
str(total_richness_per_clades, max.level = 1)
#> List of 3
#>  $ Target_clade     :List of 5
#>  $ Target_clade_name: chr [1:5] "Family_A" "Family_B" "Subfam_B1" "Gen_2" ...
#>  $ total_richness   : int [1:5] 25 NA 14 NA 8
#>  - attr(*, "richness_table")='data.frame':	5 obs. of  8 variables:

# Use it to graft the taxa
grafted_phy <- graft_missing_taxa(phy = toy_backbone, missing_taxa_list = toy_missing_taxa_list,
                                  total_richness_per_clades = total_richness_per_clades,
                                  seed = 1234, verbose = FALSE)
